draft.title: A significant person in Buddhism
card: A significant person is someone whose teaching and example shaped how Buddhism is understood or lived. Their influence can reach beyond one community or one time.
Dalai Lama
the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism. The 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, teaches compassion and non-violence, and has lived in exile in India since 1959.
Thich Nhat Hanh
a Vietnamese Zen monk who taught mindfulness in daily life and engaged Buddhism, which applies Buddhist values to social problems such as war. He helped spread Buddhism in the West.
Ashoka
an Indian emperor of the 200s BCE who turned away from war and supported Buddhist values in how he ruled. He backed the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
draft.remember: A significant person is judged by the lasting effect of their teaching and example on Buddhism.

a.q: Which description best fits Thich Nhat Hanh's contribution to Buddhism?
opts: He taught mindfulness and linked Buddhism to social issues
He ruled an empire and sent Buddhist teachers across Asia
He led Tibetan Buddhism from exile in India after 1959
He founded Buddhism by teaching the first sermon at Sarnath
a.why: Thich Nhat Hanh taught mindfulness in daily life and engaged Buddhism, which links Buddhist values to issues such as war. The option about ruling an empire describes Ashoka, and the exile option describes the Dalai Lama.
a.clue: Think of a Vietnamese Zen monk who linked mindfulness to social action.

b.q: A student says Ashoka shaped Buddhism mainly through his example as a ruler. Which evidence best supports this claim?
opts: He turned from war and backed Buddhist values in government
He taught mindfulness to Western students in retreats
He led a religious community from exile in another country
He wrote about compassion as the head of a monastic order
b.why: Ashoka's influence came from how he ruled: he turned away from war, supported Buddhist values and backed their spread. The other options describe the work of Thich Nhat Hanh, the Dalai Lama or a monastic leader, not an emperor.
b.clue: Ashoka's example came from his role as an emperor, not a monk.

a.best: He taught mindfulness and linked Buddhism to social issues

b.best: He turned from war and backed Buddhist values in government

b.q: Leo is writing an essay on Ashoka. Which statement about Ashoka's influence on Buddhism should he use?
opts: He turned from war and backed the spread of Buddhism in Asia
He waged wars of conquest so that Buddhism would spread
He taught mindfulness in daily life and helped bring it West
He taught non-violence while living in exile in India
